about: Splits, mergers and renamings of India's main political parties, 1885 to date. Compiled from the public historical record (party histories, ECI recognition orders); years only. 'eci' lists the ECI party codes under which the party appears in the Lok Sabha results, each with the years the code means this party (ECI reuses codes, e.g. SP was the Socialist Party in 1951 and the Samajwadi Party from 1996).

parties.label: Indian National Congress
parties.name: Indian National Congress
parties.note: Founded in Bombay in December 1885. After the 1969 and 1978 splits the faction led by Indira Gandhi kept the name: ECI listed it as Congress (R) in 1969–71 and Congress (I) from 1978, and simply as INC again from 1984.

parties.label: Extremists
parties.name: Extremists (Garam Dal)
parties.note: Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal's wing, separated from the Moderates at the Surat session.

parties.label: Swaraj Party
parties.name: Swaraj Party
parties.note: Formed inside Congress by C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru to contest the legislative councils.

parties.label: Congress Socialist Party
parties.name: Congress Socialist Party
parties.end_how: left Congress as the Socialist Party
parties.note: A socialist caucus inside Congress led by Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev and Ram Manohar Lohia.

parties.label: Forward Bloc
parties.name: All India Forward Bloc
parties.note: Founded by Subhas Chandra Bose after he resigned the Congress presidency. Part of the Left Front in West Bengal.

parties.label: Peasants and Workers Party
parties.name: Peasants and Workers Party of India
parties.note: Broke away from Congress in Maharashtra.

parties.label: KMPP
parties.name: Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party
parties.end_how: merged into the Praja Socialist Party
parties.note: Formed by J. B. Kripalani after he left Congress.

parties.label: Jharkhand Party
parties.name: Jharkhand Party
parties.note: Jaipal Singh's party for a Jharkhand state; merged into Congress in 1963. Splinters later revived the name.

parties.label: Kerala Congress
parties.name: Kerala Congress
parties.note: Broke away from Congress in Kerala; it has itself split many times since, e.g. Kerala Congress (M) in 1979.

parties.label: Bangla Congress
parties.name: Bangla Congress
parties.end_how: faded; its leaders returned to Congress
parties.note: Formed by Ajoy Mukherjee in West Bengal; he led the United Front governments of 1967 and 1969.

parties.label: Bharatiya Kranti Dal
parties.name: Bharatiya Kranti Dal
parties.end_how: merged into the Bharatiya Lok Dal
parties.note: Charan Singh's party after he left Congress in Uttar Pradesh.

parties.label: Utkal Congress
parties.name: Utkal Congress
parties.end_how: merged into the Bharatiya Lok Dal
parties.note: Biju Patnaik's breakaway from Congress in Odisha.

parties.label: Congress (O)
parties.name: Congress (Organisation)
parties.note: The old guard (Morarji Desai, K. Kamaraj, S. Nijalingappa) after the party expelled Indira Gandhi in 1969; her side, Congress (R), kept the bulk of the party.

parties.label: CFD
parties.name: Congress for Democracy
parties.note: Jagjivan Ram, H. N. Bahuguna and Nandini Satpathy left Congress weeks before the 1977 election; it fought on the BLD symbol with the Janata parties.

parties.label: Congress (U) / (Socialist)
parties.name: Congress (U) / Indian Congress (Socialist)
parties.note: The part of Congress that did not follow Indira Gandhi in 1978, led from 1979 by Devaraj Urs and later by Sharad Pawar, who took most of it back to Congress in 1986.

parties.label: Jan Morcha
parties.name: Jan Morcha
parties.note: V. P. Singh's platform after he was expelled from Congress.

parties.label: Haryana Vikas Party
parties.name: Haryana Vikas Party
parties.note: Bansi Lal's party after he left Congress.

parties.label: Tamil Maanila Congress
parties.name: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar)
parties.note: G. K. Moopanar's breakaway, formed when Congress allied with the AIADMK.

parties.label: Tamil Maanila Congress (revived)
parties.name: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar), revived
parties.note: Revived by G. K. Vasan after he left Congress.

parties.label: Trinamool Congress
parties.name: All India Trinamool Congress
parties.note: Formed by Mamata Banerjee in West Bengal.

parties.label: NCP
parties.name: Nationalist Congress Party
parties.note: Formed by Sharad Pawar, P. A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar after they were expelled from Congress. In February 2024 ECI recognised Ajit Pawar's faction as the NCP.

parties.label: NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)
parties.name: Nationalist Congress Party – Sharadchandra Pawar
parties.note: Name allotted to Sharad Pawar's faction after ECI awarded the NCP name and clock symbol to Ajit Pawar's faction.

parties.label: PDP
parties.name: Jammu & Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party
parties.note: Formed by Mufti Mohammad Sayeed after he left Congress.

parties.label: Haryana Janhit Congress
parties.name: Haryana Janhit Congress (BL)
parties.note: Kuldeep Bishnoi's party after he left Congress.

parties.label: YSR Congress
parties.name: YSR Congress Party
parties.note: Formed by Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy after he left Congress in Andhra Pradesh.

parties.label: AINRC
parties.name: All India N.R. Congress
parties.note: N. Rangasamy's breakaway from Congress in Puducherry.

parties.label: National People's Party
parties.name: National People's Party
parties.note: Formed by P. A. Sangma after he left the NCP; based in Meghalaya and the North-East.

parties.label: Punjab Lok Congress
parties.name: Punjab Lok Congress
parties.note: Amarinder Singh's party after he resigned as Punjab chief minister and left Congress.

parties.label: Ram Rajya Parishad
parties.name: Akhil Bharatiya Ram Rajya Parishad
parties.note: Founded by Swami Karpatri; a minor force after the 1960s.

parties.label: Jana Sangh
parties.name: Bharatiya Jana Sangh
parties.note: Founded by Syama Prasad Mookerjee in October 1951.

parties.label: BJP
parties.name: Bharatiya Janata Party
parties.note: Founded in April 1980 by former Jana Sangh members who left the Janata Party, with Atal Bihari Vajpayee as president.

parties.label: JVM (Prajatantrik)
parties.name: Jharkhand Vikas Morcha (Prajatantrik)
parties.note: Babulal Marandi's party after he left the BJP.

parties.label: Karnataka Janata Paksha
parties.name: Karnataka Janata Paksha
parties.note: B. S. Yediyurappa's party after he left the BJP; it contested the 2013 Karnataka election.

parties.label: Socialist Party
parties.name: Socialist Party
parties.end_how: merged into the Praja Socialist Party

parties.label: Praja Socialist Party
parties.name: Praja Socialist Party
parties.note: Merger of the Socialist Party and the KMPP. A merger with Lohia's socialists in 1964 broke down the next year and the PSP carried on separately.

parties.label: Socialist Party (Lohia)
parties.name: Socialist Party (Lohia)
parties.end_how: merged into the Samyukta Socialist Party
parties.note: Ram Manohar Lohia's breakaway from the PSP.

parties.label: Socialist Party
parties.name: Socialist Party
parties.note: Reunion of the PSP and SSP after the 1971 election; George Fernandes became its chairman.

parties.label: Ganatantra Parishad
parties.name: Ganatantra Parishad
parties.note: Party of Odisha's former princely rulers.

parties.label: Swatantra Party
parties.name: Swatantra Party
parties.end_how: merged into the Bharatiya Lok Dal
parties.note: Free-market party founded by C. Rajagopalachari, N. G. Ranga and Minoo Masani; the main opposition in 1967.

parties.label: Bharatiya Lok Dal
parties.name: Bharatiya Lok Dal
parties.note: Charan Singh's merger of the BKD, Swatantra, Utkal Congress, part of the SSP and smaller groups. The Janata alliance fought the 1977 election on the BLD symbol.

parties.label: Janata Party
parties.name: Janata Party
parties.note: Merger of Congress (O), the Jana Sangh, the BLD, the Socialist Party and the CFD; it won the 1977 election (ECI lists its 295 seats under BLD). After most of it joined the Janata Dal in 1988, a rump under Subramanian Swamy carried on until it merged into the BJP.

parties.label: Janata (S) / Lok Dal
parties.name: Janata Party (Secular) / Lok Dal
parties.note: Charan Singh's breakaway that brought down the Morarji Desai government; renamed Lok Dal after the 1980 election.

parties.label: Janata Dal
parties.name: Janata Dal
parties.note: Formed in October 1988 under V. P. Singh; led the National Front government of 1989 and the United Front governments of 1996–98.

parties.label: Samajwadi Janata Party (R)
parties.name: Samajwadi Janata Party (Rashtriya)
parties.note: Chandra Shekhar's breakaway from the Janata Dal; he was prime minister in 1990–91.

parties.label: Samajwadi Party
parties.name: Samajwadi Party
parties.note: Formed by Mulayam Singh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh.

parties.label: Samata Party
parties.name: Samata Party
parties.end_how: merged into JD(U) (a rump kept the name)
parties.note: George Fernandes and Nitish Kumar's breakaway from the Janata Dal, first called Janata Dal (George).

parties.label: INLD
parties.name: Indian National Lok Dal
parties.note: Devi Lal's Haryana party, first called Haryana Lok Dal (Rashtriya).

parties.label: RLD
parties.name: Rashtriya Lok Dal
parties.note: Ajit Singh's party in western Uttar Pradesh.

parties.label: RJD
parties.name: Rashtriya Janata Dal
parties.note: Lalu Prasad Yadav's breakaway from the Janata Dal in July 1997.

parties.label: Lok Shakti
parties.name: Lok Shakti
parties.note: Ramakrishna Hegde's party after his expulsion from the Janata Dal.

parties.label: BJD
parties.name: Biju Janata Dal
parties.note: Formed by Naveen Patnaik in Odisha, named after his father Biju Patnaik.

parties.label: JD(S)
parties.name: Janata Dal (Secular)
parties.note: H. D. Deve Gowda's faction when the Janata Dal split over support for the NDA.

parties.label: JD(U)
parties.name: Janata Dal (United)
parties.note: Sharad Yadav's faction of the Janata Dal with Lok Shakti; the Samata Party merged in 2003.

parties.label: Lok Janshakti Party
parties.name: Lok Janshakti Party
parties.end_how: split into LJP (Ram Vilas) and RLJP
parties.note: Ram Vilas Paswan's breakaway from JD(U).

parties.label: RLSP
parties.name: Rashtriya Lok Samta Party
parties.note: Upendra Kushwaha's party after he left JD(U).

parties.label: HAM (Secular)
parties.name: Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular)
parties.note: Jitan Ram Manjhi's party after he left JD(U).

parties.label: Jannayak Janta Party
parties.name: Jannayak Janta Party
parties.note: Dushyant Chautala's breakaway from the INLD.

parties.label: LJP (Ram Vilas)
parties.name: Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas)
parties.note: Chirag Paswan's faction; ECI froze the LJP name and symbol in 2021 and gave each faction a new name.

parties.label: Rashtriya LJP
parties.name: Rashtriya Lok Janshakti Party
parties.note: Pashupati Kumar Paras's faction of the LJP.

parties.label: CPI
parties.name: Communist Party of India
parties.note: Dates its founding to the Kanpur conference of December 1925; the CPI(M) dates it to an emigré group formed in Tashkent in 1920.

parties.label: RSP
parties.name: Revolutionary Socialist Party
parties.note: Grew out of the Anushilan Samiti revolutionaries of Bengal.

parties.label: SUCI(C)
parties.name: Socialist Unity Centre of India (Communist)
parties.note: Founded by Shibdas Ghosh.

parties.label: CPI(M)
parties.name: Communist Party of India (Marxist)
parties.note: Split from the CPI in 1964, broadly along the Sino-Soviet divide.

parties.label: CPI(ML)
parties.name: CPI (Marxist–Leninist)
parties.end_how: fragmented; the main line reorganised as CPI(ML) Liberation
parties.note: Formed by Charu Majumdar and others from the Naxalbari uprising, breaking with the CPI(M).

parties.label: CPI(ML) Liberation
parties.name: CPI (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation
parties.note: Contested through its open front, the Indian People's Front, until it entered elections under its own name.

parties.label: Justice Party
parties.name: Justice Party (South Indian Liberal Federation)
parties.note: Non-Brahmin party that governed Madras Presidency for most of 1920–37.

parties.label: Dravidar Kazhagam
parties.name: Dravidar Kazhagam
parties.note: Periyar E. V. Ramasamy's movement; it does not contest elections.

parties.label: DMK
parties.name: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
parties.note: Formed by C. N. Annadurai, who broke with Periyar; it first contested in 1957.

parties.label: AIADMK
parties.name: All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
parties.note: Formed by M. G. Ramachandran after his expulsion from the DMK.

parties.label: MDMK
parties.name: Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
parties.note: Vaiko's breakaway from the DMK.

parties.label: Muslim League
parties.name: All-India Muslim League
parties.end_how: split by Partition; reconstituted in India as the IUML
parties.note: Founded in Dhaka; led the movement for Pakistan.

parties.label: IUML
parties.name: Indian Union Muslim League
parties.note: Reconstituted in Madras in March 1948; strongest in Kerala.

parties.label: AIMIM
parties.name: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen
parties.note: Founded in Hyderabad State in 1927; revived in its present form in 1958.

parties.label: Shiromani Akali Dal
parties.name: Shiromani Akali Dal
parties.note: The Sikh party of Punjab; it has split into rival Akali Dals many times.

parties.label: National Conference
parties.name: Jammu & Kashmir National Conference
parties.note: Founded by Sheikh Abdullah as the Muslim Conference; renamed National Conference in 1939.

parties.label: Scheduled Castes Federation
parties.name: Scheduled Castes Federation
parties.end_how: succeeded by the Republican Party of India
parties.note: Founded by B. R. Ambedkar.

parties.label: Republican Party of India
parties.name: Republican Party of India
parties.note: Formed by Ambedkar's followers after his death; it has split into many factions, e.g. RPI (Athawale).

parties.label: Mizo National Front
parties.name: Mizo National Front
parties.note: Laldenga's movement; an armed insurgency until the 1986 Mizo Accord, then a party.

parties.label: Shiv Sena
parties.name: Shiv Sena
parties.note: Founded by Bal Thackeray in Bombay. In February 2023 ECI awarded the name and bow-and-arrow symbol to Eknath Shinde's faction.

parties.label: MNS
parties.name: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena
parties.note: Raj Thackeray's breakaway from the Shiv Sena.

parties.label: Shiv Sena (UBT)
parties.name: Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray)
parties.note: Uddhav Thackeray's faction after Eknath Shinde's revolt in June 2022.

parties.label: JMM
parties.name: Jharkhand Mukti Morcha
parties.note: Founded by Shibu Soren, Binod Bihari Mahato and A. K. Roy.

parties.label: TDP
parties.name: Telugu Desam Party
parties.note: Founded by N. T. Rama Rao; it won Andhra Pradesh within nine months.

parties.label: TRS / BRS
parties.name: Telangana Rashtra Samithi / Bharat Rashtra Samithi
parties.note: Formed by K. Chandrashekar Rao after he left the TDP; renamed Bharat Rashtra Samithi in 2022.

parties.label: BSP
parties.name: Bahujan Samaj Party
parties.note: Founded by Kanshi Ram.

parties.label: Sikkim Sangram Parishad
parties.name: Sikkim Sangram Parishad
parties.note: Nar Bahadur Bhandari's party.

parties.label: AGP
parties.name: Asom Gana Parishad
parties.note: Formed by leaders of the Assam movement after the 1985 Assam Accord.

parties.label: SDF
parties.name: Sikkim Democratic Front
parties.note: Pawan Chamling's breakaway from the Sikkim Sangram Parishad; it governed Sikkim from 1994 to 2019.

parties.label: AAP
parties.name: Aam Aadmi Party
parties.note: Formed by Arvind Kejriwal out of the India Against Corruption movement.

parties.label: SKM
parties.name: Sikkim Krantikari Morcha
parties.note: Prem Singh Tamang's breakaway from the SDF; in power in Sikkim since 2019.

events.text: Surat split: the Extremists and Moderates part ways at the Congress session.
Lucknow session: the Extremists return to Congress.
C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru form the Swaraj Party to enter the councils.
The Swarajists fold back into Congress.
Socialists form the Congress Socialist Party inside Congress.
Subhas Chandra Bose leaves the Congress presidency and forms the Forward Bloc.
Under Periyar the Justice Party becomes the Dravidar Kazhagam.
Peasants and Workers Party breaks away in Maharashtra.
The socialists leave Congress and form the Socialist Party.
After Partition the League's Indian members reconstitute it as the Indian Union Muslim League.
C. N. Annadurai breaks with Periyar and founds the DMK.
J. B. Kripalani leaves Congress and forms the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
The Socialist Party and KMPP merge as the Praja Socialist Party.
Ram Manohar Lohia leaves the PSP.
After Ambedkar's death the Scheduled Castes Federation becomes the Republican Party of India.
Odisha's Ganatantra Parishad merges into the Swatantra Party.
Jaipal Singh merges the Jharkhand Party into Congress.
The CPI splits; the breakaway becomes the CPI (Marxist).
Lohia's socialists and part of the PSP form the Samyukta Socialist Party; the rest of the PSP carries on.
Kerala Congress breaks away from Congress.
Ajoy Mukherjee forms the Bangla Congress in West Bengal.
Bal Thackeray founds the Shiv Sena.
Charan Singh quits Congress in Uttar Pradesh and forms the Bharatiya Kranti Dal.
Great Congress split: Indira Gandhi's Congress (R) against the old guard's Congress (O).
Biju Patnaik forms the Utkal Congress in Odisha.
Naxalite revolutionaries leave the CPI(M) and found the CPI (Marxist–Leninist).
The PSP and SSP reunite as the Socialist Party.
M. G. Ramachandran is expelled from the DMK and founds the AIADMK.
Charan Singh merges the BKD, Swatantra, Utkal Congress and smaller parties into the Bharatiya Lok Dal.
After the CPI(ML) fragments, its main line is reorganised; it later becomes CPI(ML) Liberation.
Jagjivan Ram leaves Congress and forms the Congress for Democracy.
The opposition merges into the Janata Party, which wins the post-Emergency election.
Congress splits again: Indira Gandhi's Congress (I) against the rest, later Congress (U).
Charan Singh's Janata Party (Secular) breaks away and brings down the Desai government.
Former Jana Sangh members leave the Janata Party and found the BJP.
Sharad Pawar takes most of the Indian Congress (Socialist) back into Congress.
V. P. Singh, expelled from Congress, launches the Jan Morcha.
The Janata Party, Lok Dal and Jan Morcha form the Janata Dal; a rump Janata Party continues.
After MGR's death the AIADMK splits between Janaki Ramachandran and J. Jayalalithaa; it reunites in 1989.
Chandra Shekhar breaks away and becomes prime minister with Congress support.
Bansi Lal's Haryana Vikas Party.
Mulayam Singh Yadav leaves and founds the Samajwadi Party.
Pawan Chamling forms the Sikkim Democratic Front.
George Fernandes and Nitish Kumar break away; the group becomes the Samata Party.
Vaiko is expelled from the DMK and forms the MDMK.
G. K. Moopanar's Tamil Maanila Congress opposes Congress's AIADMK alliance.
Devi Lal's Haryana Lok Dal (Rashtriya), later the INLD.
Ajit Singh's party, later the Rashtriya Lok Dal.
Lalu Prasad Yadav leaves the Janata Dal and forms the RJD.
Expelled from the Janata Dal, Ramakrishna Hegde forms Lok Shakti.
Naveen Patnaik forms the Biju Janata Dal in Odisha.
Mamata Banerjee forms the Trinamool Congress.
Sharad Pawar, P. A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar, expelled over Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin, form the NCP.
Mufti Mohammad Sayeed forms the PDP in Jammu & Kashmir.
The Janata Dal splits: Deve Gowda's JD(S) and Sharad Yadav's JD(U).
Lok Shakti joins JD(U).
Ram Vilas Paswan leaves JD(U) and forms the Lok Janshakti Party.
K. Chandrashekar Rao leaves the TDP and founds the Telangana Rashtra Samithi.
The Tamil Maanila Congress merges back into Congress.
The Samata Party merges into JD(U).
Bansi Lal merges the Haryana Vikas Party into Congress.
Raj Thackeray leaves the Shiv Sena and founds the MNS.
Babulal Marandi leaves the BJP and forms the JVM(P).
Kuldeep Bishnoi forms the Haryana Janhit Congress.
Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy forms the YSR Congress Party.
N. Rangasamy forms the All India N.R. Congress in Puducherry.
B. S. Yediyurappa leaves the BJP and forms the Karnataka Janata Paksha.
Arvind Kejriwal launches the Aam Aadmi Party.
P. A. Sangma leaves the NCP and forms the National People's Party.
Prem Singh Tamang forms the Sikkim Krantikari Morcha.
Upendra Kushwaha leaves JD(U) and forms the RLSP.
Subramanian Swamy merges the rump Janata Party into the BJP.
Yediyurappa merges the KJP back into the BJP.
G. K. Vasan leaves Congress and revives the Tamil Maanila Congress.
Jitan Ram Manjhi leaves JD(U) and forms HAM (Secular).
Kuldeep Bishnoi merges the HJC into Congress.
Dushyant Chautala breaks away from the INLD and forms the Jannayak Janta Party.
Babulal Marandi merges the JVM(P) into the BJP.
The LJP splits between Chirag Paswan and Pashupati Kumar Paras; ECI gives each faction a new name.
Upendra Kushwaha merges the RLSP into JD(U).
Amarinder Singh leaves Congress and forms the Punjab Lok Congress.
The Punjab Lok Congress merges into the BJP.
Eknath Shinde's revolt splits the Shiv Sena; ECI later recognises his faction as the Shiv Sena and Uddhav Thackeray's as Shiv Sena (UBT).
Telangana Rashtra Samithi renamed Bharat Rashtra Samithi.
After Ajit Pawar's 2023 revolt ECI recognises his faction as the NCP; Sharad Pawar's becomes NCP – Sharadchandra Pawar.
